messages:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: SSE streaming p99 spike detected for region eu-west-1. Alert: streaming.sse.tail_latency.p99 > 8s for 3m :rotating_light:
Jen (oncall): acked. i'm on it, pulling dashboards now. anyone else seeing errors from customers?
Raj (cust-ops): we started getting 10+ tickets from a few enterprise customers complaining about slow live responses (chunks arriving in bursts). One customer reported reconnects.
Miguel (sre): looking at proxy metrics — nginx write_time p95 jumped from 120ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~ 9s. TCP retransmits up on frontend LB.
Maya (eng-runtime): checking runtime traces — kv-cache hit rate normal, request queue length on model-servers stable. but output flush durations for SSE handler increased. suspect proxy or socket backpressure.
Jen (oncall): running quick health cmds: ```kubectl -n infra exec -it proxy-5f8c -- curl -sS localhost:8080/health``` returns 200, but `ss -npt | grep ESTAB | wc -l` shows many connections in CLOSE-WAIT.
Miguel (sre): stackdriver/metrics: streaming.sse.chunk_interval.p999 = 15s for eu-west-1, baseline ~100ms. Also see increase in upstream_time on proxy logs. adding `proxy-slowwrite` tag to incident.
Maya (eng-runtime): can someone tail the proxy logs? `kubectl logs proxy-5f8c -n infra -f --since=10m | grep "write_time"`
deploy-bot: deploy started: nginx-proxy/2026.03.15-hotfix -> rolling from 5->10 replicas
Jen (oncall): i've temporarily scaled proxy replica count +3 to soak. `kubectl scale deploy/nginx-proxy --replicas=8 -n infra`
Raj (cust-ops): telling affected customers we’re investigating and scaling now. pinged customer success with expected ETA 15m.
Maya (eng-runtime): digging into proxy config: keepalive_timeout is 30s, sendfile on, proxy_buffering on. client-side slow consumers may be causing head-of-line blocking. considering toggling `proxy_buffering off` for SSE routes.
Miguel (sre): note: we saw a surge of persistent slow clients (older mobile SDK) holding sockets open and reading slowly — correlates with region. Could be client backpressure.
Jen (oncall): temporary mitigation: added rate-based limiter on streaming route to protect workers. `kubectl apply -f /tmp/streaming-rate-limit.yaml` — will limit concurrent streaming streams per IP to 10.
Maya (eng-runtime): applying `proxy_buffering off` for path `/v1/stream` on one canary proxy to test. config patch applied to proxy-9a2b.
Jen (oncall): can confirm canary proxy shows chunk_interval p99 dropped to 900ms from 15s for traffic routed to it. rolling change to rest of proxies slowly.
Miguel (sre): creating a synthetic client to emulate slow reader to validate: ```while read -r line; do sleep 2; printf "%s\n" "$line"; done < <(curl -s --no-buffer $STREAM_URL)``` results show proxy backpressure when many slow readers concurrent.
Claire (pm): customer impact: several enterprise streaming customers had degraded UX. no data loss but delayed responses. marking P1 for now until mitigations stabilize.
Raj (cust-ops): coordinated messages sent to enterprise customers: we provided workaround (shorter keepalive on SDK / upgrade recommended) and ETA for fix ~30m.
Maya (eng-runtime): follow-up plan: 1) keep `proxy_buffering off` for SSE routes 2) tune keepalive / max_conns per connection 3) add adaptive slow-consumer detection to drop extremely slow clients 4) add metrics to track slow-readers per proxy.
Miguel (sre): opened incident ticket INC-2026-452 in tracker, attaching graphs and log snippets. tagging infra and customers.
Jen (oncall): handoff to Miguel for overnight watch. i will write runbook steps in the ticket and escalate to eng-runtime if we see p99 > 5s again.
Miguel (sre): taking over oncall. summary: cause likely client backpressure + proxy buffer behaviour leading to slowwrite on proxies. mitigations applied: scaled proxies, `proxy_buffering off` on streaming path, rate limiting concurrent streams, canary validated.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: nginx-proxy updated, rollouts successful (8/8 ready)
Jen (oncall): thanks team — leaving notes in #postmortems and marking this thread for follow-up timeline collection. :white_check_mark:
Claire (pm): please add a customer-impact timeline, and prioritize adaptive slow-consumer detection in next sprint.
Miguel (sre): will follow up with RCA and assign owners. leaving handoff: Miguel -> next oncall in 6h if stable.
Raj (cust-ops): customers notified of resolution; will reopen if any report recurrence.
Jen (oncall): closing live page, but keep monitoring. last checks: p95=450ms, p99=1.1s for eu-west-1.
Maya (eng-runtime): pushed a short-term dashboard for slow-reader counts: https://dashboards.internal/streams/slow_readers?region=eu-west-1
Miguel (sre): noted for post-incident: add circuit-breaker for per-connection write latency and alert at 2s sustained.
Jen (oncall): handoff complete. signing off. :wave:
